name: Golden Lancehead
facts: Its venom is up to 5 times more potent than mainland lanceheads
Lives only on one tiny island cut off by sea-level rise 11,000 years ago
Evolved to specialize in catching migratory birds from tree branches

name: Golden-Crowned Snake
facts: Despite being venomous, bites are rare and only happen when handled
It is the largest species in the crowned snake genus
Has a distinct pale yellow-brown crown-like marking on its head

name: Sydney Funnel-Web Spider
facts: Before antivenom in 1981, it caused multiple human deaths - none since!
Males have MORE potent venom for humans than females
Builds burrows with silk trip-lines to detect passing prey

name: Saltwater Crocodile
facts: Has the most powerful bite of any animal - 3,700 PSI!
Can travel hundreds of kilometers through the ocean using currents
Australian populations recovered to 100,000-200,000 after hunting bans

name: Jaguar
facts: Has a bite powerful enough to pierce turtle shells and crocodile skulls
Black jaguars (melanistic) are fairly common in dense forests
The largest cat in the Americas and third largest in the world

name: Tiger Snake
facts: Venom combines 4 deadly effects: neurotoxic, myotoxic, hemolytic, and coagulant
Responsible for many serious snakebites in southern Australia
Excellent swimmer and capable climber despite living in wetlands

name: Red-Bellied Black Snake
facts: Despite being commonly encountered, there are ZERO confirmed human deaths!
Has a gorgeous glossy black back with a bright red to pink belly
Often confused with the more dangerous eastern brown snake

name: Cheetah
facts: The fastest land animal - can reach 100-120 km/h in just 3 seconds!
Uses its long tail like a rudder for balance during high-speed chases
Unlike most big cats, cheetahs can purr and make bird-like chirping calls

name: Snow Leopard
facts: Only 4,000-6,500 remain in the wild, living in remote mountain terrain
Has an exceptionally long thick tail for balance AND to cover its face when sleeping
Home ranges can exceed 1,000 square kilometers in low-prey regions

name: Inland Taipan
facts: The most venomous snake on Earth - one bite could kill 100+ adults!
Changes color with the seasons - darker in winter to absorb more heat
Despite its power, it's extremely shy and human bites are very rare

name: Cottonmouth
facts: Named for the white interior of its mouth shown in its gaping threat display
One of the few semi-aquatic venomous snakes in North America
Many harmless water snakes are killed by mistake because they look similar

name: Alligator Snapping Turtle
facts: The largest freshwater turtle in North America - can weigh 100 kg!
Has a worm-like tongue tip it wiggles to lure fish into its jaws
Can stay underwater for 40-50 minutes without coming up for air

name: Death Adder
facts: Has the fastest strike of any snake in Australia
Uses its grub-like tail tip as a lure to attract prey
Unlike most snakes, it ambushes prey instead of hunting actively

name: Green Anaconda
facts: The heaviest snake in the world - can weigh over 200 kg!
Kills by constriction, squeezing prey until it can't breathe
Spends most of its time in water where its massive body is more mobile

name: Leafy Sea Dragon
facts: Not dangerous but extraordinarily weird - looks exactly like floating seaweed!
Males carry the eggs attached to their tail until they hatch
Can only be found in the waters off southern and western Australia

name: Black Mamba
facts: The fastest snake in the world - can slither at 20 km/h!
Named for the ink-black inside of its mouth, not its body color
Without antivenom, its bite is almost 100% fatal within 7-15 hours

name: King Cobra
facts: The longest venomous snake in the world - can reach 5.5 meters!
Can raise up to 1/3 of its body off the ground to look you in the eye
One of the only snakes that builds a nest and guards its eggs

name: Gaboon Viper
facts: Has the longest fangs of any snake - up to 5 cm long!
Injects more venom in a single bite than any other snake
Its geometric pattern provides perfect camouflage among fallen leaves

name: Eastern Brown Snake
facts: Responsible for the most snakebite deaths in Australia
The second most venomous land snake in the world
Often found near farms and houses hunting mice and rats

name: Fer-de-Lance
facts: Causes more human deaths than any other snake in the Americas
Name means 'spearhead' in French, describing its triangular head
Can give birth to up to 100 baby snakes at once!

name: Boomslang
facts: Has enormous eyes that give it excellent depth perception for hunting
Its venom prevents blood from clotting, causing internal bleeding
Name means 'tree snake' in Afrikaans

name: Blue Poison Dart Frog
facts: Its stunning blue color warns predators: 'I am TOXIC!'
One frog has enough poison to kill 10 adult humans
Loses its toxicity in captivity because the poison comes from its diet

name: Golden Poison Frog
facts: The most poisonous vertebrate on Earth!
One frog has enough toxin to kill 10-20 adult humans or 10,000 mice
Indigenous people use its poison on blowgun darts for hunting

name: Strawberry Poison Frog
facts: Nicknamed 'blue jeans frog' for its red body and blue legs
Comes in over 30 different color variations across its range
Males wrestle each other and carry tadpoles on their backs

name: Dyeing Dart Frog
facts: Legend says natives rubbed it on parrots to change their feather colors
One of the largest poison dart frogs at 5 cm long
Females compete for males - the opposite of most frogs!

name: Green & Black Poison Frog
facts: Despite its name, it can be green, blue, or even bronze colored
Males are devoted dads who carry tadpoles to water pools
One of the most commonly kept poison frogs in captivity

name: Phantasmal Poison Frog
facts: Scientists discovered a powerful painkiller from its skin toxin
Critically endangered with only a few hundred left in the wild
Its toxin is 200 times more potent than morphine!

name: Splash-Back Poison Frog
facts: Named for the bright yellow 'splash' pattern on its back
Lives only in small streams in cloud forest mountains
Both parents work together to raise their tadpoles

name: Lion
facts: The only cats that live in social groups called prides
A lion's roar can be heard from 8 kilometers away!
Female lions do 90% of the hunting for the pride

name: Tiger
facts: The largest wild cat in the world - can weigh over 300 kg!
Every tiger has unique stripes like human fingerprints
Can eat up to 40 kg of meat in one sitting

name: Leopard
facts: Can carry prey twice its own weight up into trees
The most adaptable big cat - lives in forests, mountains, and deserts
Black leopards (panthers) are the same species with extra melanin

name: Clouded Leopard
facts: Has the longest canine teeth relative to body size of any cat
Can climb down trees headfirst like a squirrel
So secretive that scientists know very little about wild behavior

name: Amur Leopard
facts: The rarest big cat in the world - only about 100 left in the wild!
Has a thicker coat than other leopards to survive freezing winters
Can leap over 6 meters horizontally and 3 meters vertically

name: Gray Wolf
facts: Packs can take down prey 10 times their size through teamwork
Can travel 50 km in a single day while hunting
Their howls can be heard from 16 km away in open terrain

name: African Wild Dog
facts: Has an 80% hunting success rate - lions only succeed 30% of the time!
Each dog has a unique coat pattern like a fingerprint
The whole pack helps feed sick or injured members

name: Dhole
facts: Communicates with whistles instead of howls - sounds like a bird!
Packs can drive away tigers and leopards from their kills
Can jump over 2 meters high from standing still

name: Arctic Fox
facts: Changes color with seasons - white in winter, brown in summer
Can survive temperatures as low as -50 degrees Celsius!
Follows polar bears to eat their leftover scraps

name: Great White Shark
facts: Can detect one drop of blood in 100 liters of water!
Has 300 triangular teeth arranged in several rows
Can breach completely out of the water when hunting seals

name: Whale Shark
facts: The largest fish in the world - can grow to 12 meters long!
Despite its size, it only eats tiny plankton and small fish
Each whale shark has a unique spot pattern like a fingerprint

name: Hammerhead Shark
facts: Its wide head gives it 360-degree vision - can see above AND below!
Uses its head to pin stingrays to the ocean floor
Swims in schools of up to 500 sharks during the day

name: Bull Shark
facts: Can swim in both salt AND fresh water - found in rivers!
Responsible for most shark attacks near shore
Has been found 4,000 km up the Amazon River

name: Tiger Shark
facts: Will eat almost anything - license plates have been found in their stomachs!
Named for the dark stripes on its body that fade with age
Second only to great whites in number of human attacks

name: Orca
facts: Actually a dolphin, not a whale - the largest dolphin species!
Different pods have different 'languages' and hunting techniques
Can hunt great white sharks by flipping them upside down

name: Humpback Whale
facts: Males sing complex songs that can last for hours!
Migrates up to 25,000 km per year - the longest of any mammal
Creates 'bubble nets' to trap fish before eating them

name: Blue Whale
facts: The largest animal that has EVER existed - bigger than any dinosaur!
Its heart is the size of a small car and weighs 400 kg
A baby blue whale gains 90 kg PER DAY drinking its mother's milk

name: Sperm Whale
facts: Can dive to 2,000 meters deep and hold its breath for 90 minutes!
Has the largest brain of any animal - 9 kg!
Hunts giant squid in the pitch-black deep ocean

name: Bottlenose Dolphin
facts: Can recognize themselves in mirrors - one of few animals to do so!
Uses echolocation to 'see' with sound underwater
Dolphins call each other by name using unique whistles

name: Stonefish
facts: The most venomous fish in the world!
Looks exactly like a rock - impossible to see until stepped on
Its sting is so painful that victims have begged to have their legs amputated

name: Lionfish
facts: Has venomous spines that cause extreme pain but are rarely fatal
An invasive species devastating Atlantic reef fish populations
A single female can release 2 million eggs per year!

name: Box Jellyfish
facts: Has enough venom to kill 60 adult humans!
Has 24 eyes but no brain - it can still see and hunt
Almost transparent - nearly invisible in the water

name: Blue-Ringed Octopus
facts: Small enough to fit in your palm but can kill 26 adults!
Blue rings only appear when it's about to attack
There is no antivenom - survival requires artificial breathing until venom wears off

name: Golden Eagle
facts: Can dive at speeds over 240 km/h to catch prey!
Has eyesight 8 times sharper than a human
About 500 pairs live in the Scottish Highlands

name: Red Kite
facts: Was almost extinct in the UK - saved by one of the world's longest conservation programs
In medieval times, they flew over London scavenging scraps
Has a distinctive forked tail that acts like a rudder in flight

name: Peregrine Falcon
facts: The fastest animal on Earth - can dive at over 380 km/h!
Was almost wiped out by pesticides but has made an amazing comeback
Now nests on skyscrapers and bridges in cities like London

name: Barn Owl
facts: Can hunt in complete darkness using only its hearing
Its face acts like a satellite dish to collect sounds
Flies completely silently thanks to special feathers

name: Atlantic Puffin
facts: Can hold over 10 fish in its beak at once to feed its chick
Spends most of its life at sea, only coming to land to breed
Flaps its wings 400 times per minute when flying!

name: Common Kingfisher
facts: Dives into water at 40 km/h to catch fish
Its feathers aren't actually blue - it's a light trick called iridescence
Eats its own body weight in fish every day

name: Mute Swan
facts: Can break a human arm with its powerful wings when defending its nest!
In the UK, all unmarked mute swans belong to the Queen
Mates for life and can live over 20 years

name: Electric Eel
facts: Can generate 860 volts - enough to knock down a horse!
Not actually an eel - more closely related to catfish
80% of its body is made up of electricity-producing organs

name: Mantis Shrimp
facts: Punches so fast it creates a shockwave that can boil water!
Has 16 types of color receptors - humans only have 3
Can break aquarium glass with its powerful strike

name: Cone Snail
facts: Fires a venomous harpoon tooth at prey - there's no antivenom!
Its beautiful shell makes it deadly - people pick them up and get stung
Scientists use its venom to develop new painkillers

name: Red-Eyed Tree Frog
facts: Not poisonous! Its bright colors are a bluff to startle predators
Sleeps with eyes closed, hiding red eyes under green eyelids
Can jump over 20 times its own body length

name: Tomato Frog
facts: Puffs up like a tomato and secretes a sticky glue when threatened
Only found on the island of Madagascar
Females are bright red while males are duller yellow-orange

name: Cane Toad
facts: Secretes bufotoxin from glands - deadly to most predators!
Introduced to Australia in 1935 and became an ecological disaster
Can eat almost anything including pet food and garbage

name: Cougar
facts: Has the largest range of any wild cat - from Canada to Argentina!
Cannot roar like big cats - instead they scream, hiss, and purr
Can leap 5.5 meters straight up from standing

name: Ocelot
facts: Salvador Dali kept an ocelot as a pet named Babou
Each ocelot has a unique pattern like a fingerprint
Excellent swimmers and climbers - truly versatile hunters

name: Brazilian Wandering Spider
facts: Considered the world's most venomous spider by Guinness Records!
Wanders the jungle floor at night instead of building webs
Sometimes hides in banana shipments, surprising workers worldwide

name: Black Widow Spider
facts: Venom is 15 times stronger than a rattlesnake's!
Named because females sometimes eat males after mating
The red hourglass marking warns predators of its deadly nature

name: Brown Recluse Spider
facts: Its bite causes necrosis - flesh literally dies and rots away
Has only 6 eyes instead of the usual 8 for spiders
True to its name, it's extremely shy and rarely bites

name: Redback Spider
facts: Responsible for more antivenom doses than any other creature in Australia
Loves hiding in outdoor toilets - watch where you sit!
Female is 10 times larger than the male

name: Goliath Birdeater
facts: The largest spider by mass - can weigh 175 grams!
Leg span can reach 30 cm - the size of a dinner plate
Despite its name, it rarely eats birds - prefers insects and frogs

name: Camel Spider
facts: Not actually a spider - belongs to a group called solifuges
Can run up to 16 km/h - one of the fastest arachnids!
Has massive jaws that make up 1/3 of its body length

name: Deathstalker Scorpion
facts: The most dangerous scorpion in the world!
Its venom is worth $39 million per gallon for medical research
Glows bright blue-green under ultraviolet light

name: Emperor Scorpion
facts: One of the largest scorpions but has very mild venom
Popular as a pet because of its docile nature
Mothers carry babies on their backs for weeks after birth

name: Arizona Bark Scorpion
facts: The most venomous scorpion in North America!
Can climb walls, trees, and even hang upside down from ceilings
Stings cause intense pain for 24-72 hours

name: Harpy Eagle
facts: Has talons the size of grizzly bear claws!
The most powerful eagle in the world - can lift prey equal to its weight
Named after the harpies of Greek mythology

name: Cassowary
facts: Has a 12 cm dagger-like claw that can disembowel with one kick!
Considered the most dangerous bird in the world
Its helmet-like casque may help it hear low-frequency sounds

name: Secretary Bird
facts: Kicks with 5 times its own body weight - enough to shatter bones!
Specializes in hunting venomous snakes including cobras
Named for its quill-like head feathers resembling old-time clerks

name: Shortfin Mako Shark
facts: The fastest shark in the ocean - can reach 74 km/h!
Can leap up to 6 meters out of the water
Has been clocked at bursts of up to 96 km/h

name: Goblin Shark
facts: Its lineage dates back 125 million years - older than dinosaurs!
Has a jaw that shoots forward like a slingshot to catch prey
Lives so deep it's pink because blood vessels show through its skin

name: Thresher Shark
facts: Uses its incredibly long tail to whip and stun fish!
Tail can be as long as its entire body
One of the only sharks that can breach completely out of water

name: Oceanic Whitetip Shark
facts: Blamed for more human deaths than all other sharks combined!
Historically attacked survivors of ship and plane wrecks
Jacques Cousteau called it 'the most dangerous of all sharks'

name: Blue Shark
facts: Migrates farther than any other shark - up to 9,000 km!
Has a stunning indigo blue color on its back
Can have litters of over 100 pups at once

name: Golden-Tailed Gecko
facts: Can squirt sticky, smelly fluid from glands in its tail to scare off predators!
Its tail is covered in tiny golden spines that give it a shimmering appearance
Unlike most geckos, it lives in trees and shrubs rather than on rocks or walls

name: Cardboard Frog
facts: Males carry their tadpoles in special hip pouches - the only frog in the world to do this!
One of the smallest frogs in Australia at only 2 cm long
Also called the hip-pocket frog because of its amazing dad-pouch superpower

name: Frill-Necked Lizard
facts: Opens a huge colorful frill around its neck to look bigger and scare predators!
Can run on its two back legs at high speed - like a tiny dinosaur!
Featured on the Australian 2-cent coin before it was discontinued

name: Blue Banded Bee
facts: Has stunning metallic blue stripes instead of the usual yellow - nature's punk rocker!
Buzz pollinates flowers by vibrating 350 times per second - that helps grow better tomatoes!
Unlike honeybees, it's a solitary bee that builds its own tiny mud nest

name: Green Tree Python
facts: Babies are born bright yellow or red and turn vivid green as they grow up!
Drapes its body in perfect coils over branches like a living necklace
Uses heat-sensing pits along its lips to detect warm-blooded prey in total darkness

name: Bulloak Jewel Butterfly
facts: One of Australia's rarest butterflies - critically endangered with very few left!
Can only survive if both bulloak trees AND a specific species of ant are present
Its caterpillars are adopted by ants and raised inside their nests like secret guests!

name: Tree Iguana
facts: Can fall 15 meters from a tree and land without getting hurt!
Excellent swimmers that can hold their breath underwater for up to 30 minutes
Has a third eye on top of its head that senses light and shadows from above

name: Blue-Tongued Lizard
facts: Flashes its bright blue tongue to startle and confuse predators - surprise!
One of the most commonly found reptiles in Australian backyards and gardens
Gives birth to live babies instead of laying eggs - up to 25 at a time!

name: Australian Tiger Moth
facts: Some species can produce ultrasound clicks to jam bat sonar - like a stealth fighter!
Has bright warning colors that tell predators: 'I taste TERRIBLE!'
Its hairy caterpillars can cause skin irritation if you touch them

name: Red Hornet
facts: Delivers an incredibly painful sting that can cause severe allergic reactions!
Can be extremely aggressive when defending their nest as a swarm
Their nests can house thousands of hornets working together like a tiny angry army

name: Indian Red Scorpion
facts: Considered one of the most lethal scorpions in the world!
Its venom can cause fluid to fill the lungs - called pulmonary edema
Despite its name, it ranges from orange to brown and is not always red

name: Fattail Scorpion
facts: Its scientific name Androctonus literally means 'man-killer' in Greek!
Responsible for the majority of scorpion-related deaths in North Africa
Has a thick, powerful tail that can deliver venom with lightning speed

name: Striped Bark Scorpion
facts: The most commonly encountered scorpion in the United States!
Loves hiding in shoes, clothing, and bedding - always shake before wearing!
Glows a bright blue-green under ultraviolet light like a tiny alien

name: Yellow Scorpion
facts: Its pale yellow color is perfect camouflage against desert sand!
Can survive for months without food by slowing its metabolism to a crawl
Has special comb-like organs on its belly that sense vibrations in the ground

name: Amazonian Green-Horned Centipede
facts: Climbs walls and cave ceilings to snatch bats right out of the air
Uses its back legs to anchor to surfaces while its front body dangles to catch flying prey
Recently documented by scientists on ResearchGate hunting bats in wooden structures and caves

name: Giant Desert Centipede
facts: Observed in Palo Duro Canyon, Texas, preying on bats hiding in rock crevices
The largest centipede in North America, reaching up to 20 cm long
Has a painful venomous bite that causes intense swelling and pain lasting for days

name: Amazonian Giant Centipede
facts: The largest centipede in the world at 30 cm — it hangs from cave ceilings to catch flying bats
The only centipede species confirmed to have caused a human death
Can kill and eat tarantulas, snakes, lizards, frogs, birds, and mice

name: Vietnamese Centipede
facts: Can kill a mouse 15 times its own weight in just 30 seconds using 'Spooky Toxin'
Its venom simultaneously shuts down the heart, lungs, muscles, and nervous system
A specimen found in Hawaii measured 36.6 cm — possibly the largest individual centipede ever

name: Asian Forest Centipede
facts: Strikes faster than the human eye can track — from motionless to full speed in an instant
Its venom contains cardiotoxin that can cause tissue death and severe allergic reactions
Actively patrols its territory at night rather than waiting in ambush like other centipedes

name: Australian Giant Centipede
facts: One of the few native predators that can kill and eat the deadly invasive cane toad
Uses extra-oral digestion — its venom dissolves prey tissues before it even starts eating
Australia's largest centipede, with bite pain described as extreme and lasting for days

name: Waterfall Centipede
facts: The world's first known amphibious centipede — it swims like an eel using horizontal undulations
Its body is hydrophobic so water rolls right off, leaving it completely dry when it surfaces
Only 4 specimens have ever been found, making it one of the rarest centipedes on Earth

name: Tanzanian Blue Ringleg
facts: Found on every inhabited continent — one of the most invasive centipede species on Earth
Stole genetic material from bacteria and fungi to make its venom more potent
Mothers eat their own eggs when stressed — a gruesome survival strategy called filial cannibalism

name: Caribbean Giant Centipede
facts: Attacks and eats the deadly cane toad, completely immune to its powerful bufotoxin
The largest centipede found in the United States east of the Mississippi River
Uses venomous forcipules to inject venom and dissolve flesh before eating its prey

name: Megarian Banded Centipede
facts: The largest and most venomous centipede in all of Europe
Lurks under rocks and in ancient stone walls across popular Mediterranean tourist destinations
Ancient Greeks and Romans knew this species well and feared its painful bite

name: Salmon Shark
facts: Has the highest body temperature of any shark, keeping its core up to 21°C above freezing ocean water
Hunts in packs of 30-40 sharks, devouring up to 25% of Alaska's entire salmon run
Often mistaken for a Great White due to its eerily similar appearance

name: Fishing Cat
facts: The only wild cat that actively dives headfirst underwater to catch fish with its bare paws
Has semi-webbed front feet that work like built-in flippers for swimming and scooping fish
Listed as Vulnerable with fewer than 10,000 left in the wild due to rapid wetland destruction

name: Alligator Gar
facts: Can grow over 3 meters long and weigh 140 kg — the largest freshwater fish in North America
Its lineage dates back 100 million years — it literally swam alongside dinosaurs
Has a primitive swim bladder that works like a lung, letting it breathe air and survive in stagnant water

name: Piranha
facts: A group of piranhas can strip a large fish to bones in under a minute during a feeding frenzy
Despite their scary reputation, piranhas are actually shy and mostly eat smaller fish, insects, and even plants
Their razor-sharp interlocking teeth work like scissors and are so strong they were used as cutting tools by indigenous people

name: Goliath Tigerfish
facts: Has 32 razor-sharp teeth the size of a great white shark's — one of the most fearsome freshwater predators alive
Can leap out of the water to catch birds in mid-flight like a living missile
Lives in the Congo River's extreme rapids where few other predators dare to hunt

name: Payara
facts: Has two enormous fangs up to 15 cm long — so long that its upper jaw has special holes for them to fit into
Eats piranhas for breakfast, making it one of the few fish that hunts the feared piranha
Hunts in fast-moving rapids and strikes prey from below with explosive speed

name: Candiru
facts: This tiny parasitic fish is nearly invisible in the water and sneaks into the gills of bigger fish to drink their blood
Has backward-pointing spines that lock it in place once inside a host — like a living fish hook
Only 2-5 cm long but considered the most feared tiny fish in the entire Amazon River

name: Wels Catfish
facts: The largest freshwater fish in Europe — can grow over 2.7 meters long and weigh 130 kg
Has learned to beach itself on riverbanks to grab pigeons, earning it the nickname 'freshwater killer whale'
Can live for over 80 years and uses sensitive whiskers to hunt in complete darkness

name: Arapaima
facts: Has armor-plated scales so tough that piranhas cannot bite through them — nature's bulletproof vest
One of the largest freshwater fish on Earth at up to 3 meters long and 200 kg
Must breathe air like a mammal, surfacing every 10-20 minutes with a loud gulping sound

name: Giant Freshwater Stingray
facts: Might be the heaviest freshwater fish in the world — one caught in Cambodia in 2022 weighed 300 kg
Hides buried under sand on the riverbed, making it almost completely invisible to anyone wading nearby
Its venomous tail barb can be 38 cm long and delivers an excruciatingly painful sting

name: Giant Snakehead
facts: Can breathe air and survive out of water for days — it can even slither across land to reach new ponds
Nicknamed 'fishzilla' because it takes over every ecosystem it invades and eats everything
Extremely aggressive when guarding its young and will attack anything that comes close, including humans

name: Goonch Catfish
facts: Suspected of pulling people underwater in India's Kali River — investigated by famous angler Jeremy Wade
Has sharp backward-pointing teeth designed for gripping prey so nothing can escape its jaws
Some scientists think these catfish grew extra large by feeding near riverside funeral pyres

name: Nile Perch
facts: When introduced to Lake Victoria, it gobbled up over 200 native fish species — causing the biggest freshwater mass extinction ever
Can grow up to 2 meters long and 200 kg, making it one of the biggest freshwater fish in the world
Such a greedy eater that it will even cannibalize its own species when other food runs out

name: Red-bellied Pacu
facts: A close cousin of the piranha but with flat, square teeth that look disturbingly human
Its bite is strong enough to crack open Brazil nuts — one of the hardest nuts in the world
Has become an invasive species found on every continent except Antarctica after being released from aquariums

name: Bluefin Tuna
facts: Can reach speeds of 70 km/h and cross the Atlantic Ocean in under 60 days
Grows up to 3 metres long and can weigh over 900 kg — heavier than a horse
Critically endangered from overfishing, a single bluefin sold for $3.1 million at auction in Japan

name: Bullet Ant
facts: Has the most painful sting of any insect on Earth — rated 4+ on the Schmidt Pain Index, it feels like being shot by a bullet!
Can grow up to 3 cm long, making it one of the largest ants in the world — as big as your thumb!
Some tribes in Brazil use bullet ant stings as a warrior initiation — boys must wear gloves full of bullet ants for 10 minutes without crying

name: Spitting Cobra
facts: Can spit venom up to 3 metres with deadly accuracy — aiming straight for the eyes to blind its enemies!
Has special fangs with forward-facing holes designed like tiny water guns to spray venom
Unlike most cobras, it prefers to spit rather than bite — but its bite can still be fatal to humans

name: American Black Bear
facts: Can run up to 56 km/h — that's faster than a horse and way faster than any human!
Has an incredible sense of smell 7 times better than a bloodhound and can sniff food from over 30 km away
Despite their name, black bears can be brown, cinnamon, blonde, or even white — the 'spirit bear' is an all-white black bear!

name: Hawk
facts: Has eyesight 8 times sharper than humans — can spot a mouse from over 1.5 km away!
Can dive at speeds over 240 km/h to catch prey, striking with the force of a bullet
Hawks mate for life and build massive nests called 'eyries' that they return to year after year

name: Bald Eagle
facts: Has a wingspan of up to 2.3 metres — wider than most adults are tall!
Can lift fish weighing up to 1.8 kg out of the water with its powerful talons while flying at full speed
Nearly went extinct in the 1960s with only 417 pairs left, but conservation brought them back to over 300,000 — one of nature's greatest comeback stories!

name: Monitor Lizard
facts: The monitor lizard family includes the Komodo dragon — the largest lizard on Earth at over 3 metres long!
Has a forked tongue like a snake that it flicks in and out to smell prey from kilometres away
Some species are so intelligent they can count — in zoo experiments, monitors could tell the difference between groups of 3 and 4 snails!

name: Desert Horned Lizard
facts: Can shoot blood from its eyes up to 1.5 metres to scare off predators — the blood tastes disgusting to coyotes and dogs!
Covered in spiky horns and scales that make it look like a tiny dinosaur from the Cretaceous period
Can change colour to blend perfectly into desert sand and rocks — nearly invisible when it stays still

name: Saltwater Crocodile
facts: The largest living reptile on Earth — can grow over 6 metres long and weigh more than 1,000 kg!
Has the most powerful bite ever measured in any living animal at over 16,000 newtons — strong enough to crush a car!
Can swim across open ocean for hundreds of kilometres and has been found 1,000 km from the nearest coast
